sources.citation: International Handbook of Evaluated Criticality Safety Benchmark Experiments (ICSBEP), IEU-COMP-THERM-003 (2007)

kinetics.delayedGroupsSource: betas: vavtar2021 Table 1; lambdas: Keepin 1965 (vavtar2021 Table 1 gives 0.1115 and 1.1380 for groups 3 and 5)

heatCapacity.description: cp(T) = 333 + 0.678*(T - 274.15) in J/(kg*K), standard 12 wt% U element
heatCapacity.source: vavtar2021 eq. 1.8, citing Simnad, GA E-177-833 (1980)

fuelMeat.coreFuelMassKgNote: assumed 84 kg, unsourced and wrong (C2 pass 3): it equals 36 elements. svajger2024 Table 10: 2.36 kg/element (matches geometry: 382 cm3 x 6.18 g/cm3). Core 242 has 59 elements (139 kg), core 246 has 65 (154 kg), per the database core maps. Kept until the user decides on the M1 criterion; see docs/validation/m1-c1-results.md.

coreElementCounts.source: trigapulse.ijs.si core maps 242.pdf, 246.pdf (read 2026-09-27; 2 elements in the storage rack excluded)

fuelTemperaturePrompt.description: |alpha_f|(T) in 1e-5 (Delta k/k)/K, fresh fuel, linear between points, negative sign
fuelTemperaturePrompt.precision: +-0.5e-5 per K (read by eye from a figure)
fuelTemperaturePrompt.source: vavtar2021 Fig. 1 (after PULSTRI, Ravnik et al.)

crossCheck.source: svajger2024 Table 2 (Serpent, ENDF/B-VII.0, standard fuel, k-infinity)

table10Constant.source: svajger2024 Table 10 (constant used in their theoretical models; gives gamma = 2.1e-9 /J with 59 x 2.36 kg and C = 341.6)

poisons.fluxPerWattNote: n/(m^2 s) per W, core average. Was 4.0e7, which is 1000x below a typical 250 kW TRIGA (~1e12 n/(cm^2 s)) and disagreed with the library; likely a cm^2/m^2 slip. 4.0e10 is an unverified estimate matching the library (review 2026-09-26).
